newsitem.title: UK: Britain poorer without you, Major tells S. Asians.
newsitem.headline: Britain poorer without you, Major tells S. Asians.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major paid tribute on Tuesday to the contribution immigrants from the Indian sub-continent have made to Britain, telling them: "British culture would be poorer without you".

"The ledger is in credit and the British people value what South Asia has brought us," Major told 300 guests at a dinner to celebrate the 50th anniversary this year of Britain granting independence to India and Pakistan.

"The contribution of the South Asian community in Britain...strengthens the values that characterise the best in British society -- tolerance, respect for the law, enterprise, the efforts of ordinary decent people to build their family life."
Almost half of Britain's ethnic minority population of just under three million people is of Indian, Pakistani or Bangladeshi origin.

The event, attended by leaders of all the main political parties as well as representatives of British South Asian communities, was the first of a series planned to celebrate British links with the countries of the region.
They include a reception in June to be hosted by heir to the throne Prince Charles and a visit to India and Pakistan by his mother, Queen Elizabeth, in October.
Major said the use of English, membership of the Commonwealth and "the deep well of friendship built up over generations" bound Britain, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka together.

He said he believed democracy, which might sometimes have seemed a "fragile plant" in South Asia had now "firmly taken root", and praised governments of the region for liberalising their economies, following a trail blazed by Britain.
